articles.title: Delivery Boy Killed as Cement Mixer Truck Overturns Near Pune’s Navale Bridge
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 31-year-old gig worker employed as a delivery boy was killed in a tragic road accident near Navale Bridge on the Mumbai–Bengaluru Highway after a cement mixer truck allegedly lost control and overturned, police said.

body.html:
A 31-year-old gig worker employed as a delivery boy was killed in a tragic road accident near Navale Bridge on the Mumbai–Bengaluru Highway after a cement mixer truck allegedly lost control and overturned, police said.

The deceased has been identified as Rameshwar Machhindra Bhogale (31), a resident of Waghjai Nagar near Jain Mandir in Katraj and a native of Sangvi village in Beed district.

According to police, the accident occurred at around 12:30 am near Pulse Hospital in Narhe. Preliminary investigations revealed that the 16-tyre Ashok Leyland cement mixer truck (MH 12 RN 2866), driven by Gorakh Laxman Ransure (50), was travelling from Katraj towards Bavdhan when the driver allegedly lost control while negotiating a turn near Navale Bridge.

The truck overturned on the road, crushing a Honda Shine motorcycle (MH 23 BL 5225) travelling towards Bavdhan. Bhogale, who was riding the motorcycle, sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.

Another account under investigation suggests the cement-laden truck may have suffered brake failure while descending the Navale Bridge slope, causing it to crash into multiple vehicles before the fatal collision. Police are examining all possible circumstances, including mechanical failure and negligent driving.

The truck driver sustained minor head injuries and was shifted for medical treatment, while Bhogale's body was sent to Sassoon General Hospital for post-mortem examination.

The accident led to temporary traffic disruption on the busy highway stretch before police personnel and local residents cleared the damaged vehicles and restored traffic movement.

CCTV footage of the incident has surfaced and is being examined as part of the investigation.

A case has been registered at Narhe Police Station, and further legal action is underway.

The incident has once again raised concerns over the safety of the accident-prone Navale Bridge stretch, which has witnessed several serious crashes involving heavy vehicles in recent years.

articles.title: Suitcase Murder Solved: Barcode on Trousers Leads Police to Wife and Friend in Shocking Chennai Case
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a major breakthrough in the gruesome Perambur suitcase murder case, Chennai Police have arrested a woman and her friend for allegedly murdering her husband, dismembering his body and disposing of the remains at multiple locations.

body.html:
In a major breakthrough in the gruesome Perambur suitcase murder case, Chennai Police have arrested a woman and her friend for allegedly murdering her husband, dismembering his body and disposing of the remains at multiple locations.

The severed head of Ameer Ali, a native of Assam whose torso was found inside an abandoned suitcase at Perambur Railway Station on June 5, was recovered from Kolavai Lake in Chengalpattu on June 8.

The case came to light when Railway Protection Force personnel discovered a suspicious suitcase at Perambur Railway Station. Upon opening it, they found a decomposed headless torso, later identified as Ameer Ali.

Police said the investigation began with a pair of trousers found on the body. Using a barcode on the garment, investigators traced it to a shop in T. Nagar and obtained the mobile number of the purchaser.

Analysis of the phone's location data revealed frequent movement between T. Nagar and Teynampet. Further inquiries showed links to a cancer hospital in Teynampet, where staff identified a woman caregiver who regularly accompanied patients.

Investigators also recovered red and yellow plastic covers from the crime scene, which were identified as biomedical disposal bags used at a hospital in Taramani. This led police to examine records of employees who handled such materials.

Meanwhile, CCTV analysis helped investigators identify a suspicious Rapido auto-rickshaw. By tracking its movements and matching them with booking records, police traced the suspects' residence in Teynampet and arrested them.

According to police, the accused have been identified as Rahima Khatun (30), the victim's wife, and her friend Asraf Ali (36), both natives of Assam.

During interrogation, Rahima allegedly told police that she worked as a broker arranging travel and accommodation for cancer patients from other states. She claimed that her husband was involved with other women and frequently assaulted her, causing severe mental distress. Police said she had shared these allegations with Asraf Ali, after which the duo allegedly conspired to kill Ameer Ali.

Investigators said the accused allegedly mixed sleeping tablets in the victim's milk on June 2. After he lost consciousness, they allegedly slit his throat, killing him.

Police said the accused then dismembered the body, placed the headless torso inside a suitcase and abandoned it at Perambur Railway Station on June 5. During questioning, they allegedly revealed that the severed head had been concealed in the Chengalpattu area, while the arms and legs were thrown into the Buckingham Canal near their residence in Teynampet.

Based on information provided by the accused, police recovered the severed head from Kolavai Lake and later recovered the victim's arms and legs from the Buckingham Canal.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Parking Dispute Turns Violent at Udupi’s Sri Krishna Mutt: Tourist Group and Local Man File Cross-
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A minor parking dispute at the Sri Krishna Mutt parking area in Udupi escalated into a physical clash between out-of-state tourists and a local resident on the night of June 9, prompting police to register cases against both sides.

body.html:
A minor parking dispute at the Sri Krishna Mutt parking area in Udupi escalated into a physical clash between out-of-state tourists and a local resident on the night of June 9, prompting police to register cases against both sides.

According to reports, the altercation began over giving way to a vehicle in the parking zone. Tourists from Hyderabad alleged that a local car driver, identified as Supreeth, a resident of Korangrapadi, attempted to run his vehicle over them.

The tourists claimed that when they objected, a heated argument broke out, following which Supreeth allegedly assaulted them with a stick kept inside his car. Several tourists sustained injuries, and one of them, Pawan from Hyderabad, filed a complaint at the Udupi Town Police Station.

In a counter-complaint, Supreeth alleged that the tourists picked a quarrel with him after he asked them to drive slowly. He also claimed that they damaged his car's window glass and assaulted him with a chair and a photo frame stand, causing injuries and bleeding from his mouth.

The tourist group, which included women and children from Andhra Pradesh, had come to Udupi on a visit. As the argument turned into a scuffle, local residents rushed to the spot and intervened to stop the fight.

A mobile phone video of the incident has surfaced and is being examined by the police as part of the investigation.

Police have registered cross-complaints from both parties and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Senior Citizen Suffers Fractured Leg After Objecting to Spitting
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A road rage incident outside a mall in Thane turned violent after an auto-rickshaw driver allegedly assaulted a senior citizen who objected to him spitting and gargling on a public road.

body.html:
A road rage incident outside a mall in Thane turned violent after an auto-rickshaw driver allegedly assaulted a senior citizen who objected to him spitting and gargling on a public road.

According to reports, the elderly man requested the driver not to spit on the road, following which an argument broke out and quickly escalated into a physical altercation. The driver allegedly attacked the senior citizen, leaving him with serious injuries, including a fractured leg.

The injured man was rushed to a hospital, where he is currently undergoing treatment.

A video of the incident later surfaced on social media and went viral, triggering widespread outrage and demands for strict action against the accused.

In a subsequent development, two individuals claiming to be associated with a political youth wing confronted the auto driver and allegedly assaulted him before handing him over to the Vartak Nagar Police Station.

Following the viral video, local Shiv Sena workers also reportedly helped trace the accused and alerted the police.

Police have taken cognisance of both incidents and arrested the auto-rickshaw driver. A case has been registered, and investigators are examining the sequence of events based on video footage and witness statements.

Authorities have assured that appropriate legal action will be taken based on the findings.

The incident has reignited concerns over road rage, public behaviour and the safety of senior citizens in public spaces.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking case of suspected arson has come to light from the E-Block area of Jahangirpuri in Delhi, where four masked youths allegedly set several motorcycles on fire late at night.

body.html:
A shocking case of suspected arson has come to light from the E-Block area of Jahangirpuri in Delhi, where four masked youths allegedly set several motorcycles on fire late at night.

According to reports, CCTV footage of the incident shows the masked suspects entering the locality and inspecting a motorcycle parked outside a resident's house by lifting its cover.

The accused then allegedly checked other motorcycles parked nearby before deliberately setting multiple vehicles on fire.

The footage further shows the suspects remaining at the spot for some time, watching the motorcycles burn before calmly leaving the area.

Police have taken cognisance of the incident and registered an investigation. Efforts are underway to identify and trace the suspects with the help of CCTV footage and other available evidence.

The motive behind the alleged arson is yet to be determined, and further investigation is in progress.

articles.title: Retired Army Major vs Gurugram Traffic Police: Bodycam Clears Cops, But Fresh Probe Continues Over
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A complaint filed by a retired Army officer alleging harassment and misconduct by Gurugram Traffic Police during a late-night drunk-driving check has taken a new turn, with authorities stating that a preliminary investigation has found no evidence of any misbehaviour by the police...

body.html:
A complaint filed by a retired Army officer alleging harassment and misconduct by Gurugram Traffic Police during a late-night drunk-driving check has taken a new turn, with authorities stating that a preliminary investigation has found no evidence of any misbehaviour by the police personnel involved.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Prateek Gehlot said an inquiry is being conducted under the supervision of Assistant Commissioner of Police (Traffic Headquarters and Highway) Satpal Yadav into allegations that traffic personnel misbehaved with a driver and issued an incorrect challan around midnight on June 6.

According to the DCP, body-worn camera footage from the alcohol-checking operation was reviewed as part of the investigation. The footage showed that the driver was issued a challan under the Motor Vehicles Act after the breathalyser recorded an alcohol level of 91 mg/100 ml. The preliminary probe found no evidence of misconduct or misbehaviour by the Gurugram Traffic Police towards the driver or his family.

Addressing a press conference, Gehlot said the Gurugram Police Commissioner has implemented a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for alcohol checks. Under the SOP, weekly drunk-driving drives are conducted on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays between 10:00 pm and 1:00 am on roads with higher instances of drinking and driving.

He added that zonal officers are required to wear body-worn cameras during the checks to ensure transparency and that a new mouthpiece is used on the breathalyser for every driver tested.

The DCP also confirmed that the matter is being further investigated by ACP (Traffic East) Manjeet Singh.

The controversy began after retired Major Hemendra Singh filed a complaint accusing traffic police personnel of misbehaving with him and his family during a drunk-driving check on the night of June 6.

According to his complaint, he was returning home with his wife and two daughters after dinner on Cyber City Golf Course Road when they were stopped by a police team. Singh alleged that an officer used a breathalyser previously used on another driver without changing the mouthpiece, resulting in an initial reading of 91 mg/100 ml, following which he was allegedly abused and issued a challan.

The retired officer claimed that after demanding a fair re-test with a fresh mouthpiece, the police initially resisted but later conducted two additional tests. Both reportedly showed an alcohol level of 13 mg/100 ml, which he described as being within the legally permissible limit.

Singh further alleged that his family was made to stand on the roadside for nearly one and a half hours around midnight and that even after the re-test, police refused to let them leave immediately.

He said he called the emergency helpline 112 to report the incident and alleged that the traffic personnel left the spot after learning about the complaint.

In his written complaint to the Police Commissioner, Major Singh, who retired in 2007 on disability after being injured in a terrorist encounter in Jammu and Kashmir, has sought an impartial investigation into the alleged harassment.

articles.title: CCTV Captures Horror on Delhi–Jaipur Highway: Out-of-Control Trailer Runs Over Pedestrian, Man Dies
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A man lost his life in a tragic road accident in the Antela area of Kotputli after a trailer allegedly lost control during a traffic diversion and crashed into a hotel parking area on the Delhi–Jaipur Highway on 8 June 2026.

body.html:
A man lost his life in a tragic road accident in the Antela area of Kotputli after a trailer allegedly lost control during a traffic diversion and crashed into a hotel parking area on the Delhi–Jaipur Highway on 8 June 2026.

The deceased has been identified as Surjaram Yadav, who was reportedly walking near the parking area when the trailer ran over him. He died on the spot due to the impact.

The entire incident was captured on CCTV footage, which has since gone viral on social media. The video shows the trailer veering off its path and entering the hotel parking area before striking the pedestrian.

Police have seized the trailer and registered an FIR in connection with the incident.

Authorities are also investigating whether negligence in traffic diversion arrangements or ongoing road construction work contributed to the accident.

Further investigation is underway to determine the exact circumstances that led to the fatal crash.

articles.title: CCTV Captures Fatal Head-On Collision in Kerala: 60-Year-Old Biker Killed, Woman and Two Children
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic road accident in Kerala's Malappuram district claimed the life of a 60-year-old man and left three others, including two children, seriously injured after a motorcycle collided head-on with a mini van at Tanur Nadakkavu on Monday.

body.html:
A tragic road accident in Kerala's Malappuram district claimed the life of a 60-year-old man and left three others, including two children, seriously injured after a motorcycle collided head-on with a mini van at Tanur Nadakkavu on Monday.

The deceased has been identified as Akkakuzhi Iqbal (60), a resident of Kalad. The accident occurred at around 4:30 pm near Nadakkavu Junction and was captured on CCTV.

According to police and eyewitnesses, the motorcycle and the mini van collided head-on, completely destroying the two-wheeler due to the impact.

Three pillion riders travelling with Iqbal—Shahina (29), Rasha Fathima (9), and one-and-a-half-year-old Ozil—sustained serious injuries. Local residents and Tanur police rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to a private hospital in Tirur, where they are currently undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit.

The collision caused temporary traffic disruption on the Tanur-Parappanangadi road before police cleared the damaged vehicles and restored normal movement.

After completing the inquest proceedings, police shifted Iqbal's body to the district hospital mortuary for post-mortem examination.

Authorities have initiated further procedures to determine the exact circumstances that led to the accident.

The CCTV footage of the crash has circulated widely, serving as a stark reminder of the importance of road safety and the devastating consequences that can result from a single moment on the road.
